answer: Each new identity must lock a refundable copper-denominated bond before its answers count, and the bond is slashed if peers catch it copying. An attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must park a thousand bonds and keep them exposed to audits, so cost scales linearly per identity. An honest agent that does not wander into copying locks one bond once and never loses it, so only cheaters pay. Like a river fed by one source, copied answers trace back to a single origin.
